name: Burmeso
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Donohue, Mark (2001) 'Animacy, class and gender in Burmeso', in The Boy from Bundaberg (sketch with phonology section); Tasti & Donohue (1998) A Small Dictionary of Burmeso, ms

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark. 2001. Animacy, class and gender in Burmeso. In A. Pawley, M. Ross & D. Tryon (eds), The boy from Bundaberg: studies in Melanesian linguistics in honour of Tom Dutton, 97-115. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics 514.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: library print copy (Scan & Deliver or loan); the journal or volume is held, not the item itself: WID Offsite Storage PL6201.B69 2001
sources.note: Nothing. The paper is a morphosyntactic sketch (verbal/nominal/adjectival agreement, classes, gender); the only phonological remark is footnote 2 (p. 98) on the orthography (/j/ before [i] unwritten, final devoicing, word-final lowering of high vowels). No word 'stress', 'accent', 'tone', 'syllable' or 'phonology' anywhere in the 19 pages; no stress diacritics on examples.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Burmeso language' (accessed 2026-09-17), phonology tables sourced to Foley 2018.
sources.note: Consonant and vowel inventories only (from Foley 2018); nothing on stress, tone or syllable structure.

sources.citation: Clouse, Duane, Mark Donohue & Felix Ma. 2002. Survey report of the north coast of Irian Jaya. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2002-078.
sources.note: Burmeso is mentioned once (classification remark under 4.4); the report covers Masep, Yoke, Airoran, Samarokena, not Burmeso; no Burmeso stress statement.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page burm1264; Grambank page burm1264 (coder H. Hammarström; sources Donohue 2001, Lean n.d.).
sources.note: Nothing; Glottolog's only descriptive reference is Donohue 2001 (grammar_sketch).

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark. 2000. Pronouns and gender: exploring nominal classification systems in northern New Guinea. Oceanic Linguistics 39(2), section 3.1 'Burmeso'.
sources.note: Nothing; Burmeso section gives absolutive prefixes and gender/class facts only, refers to Donohue (in press = 2001) for details.

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark. 1997. Tone in New Guinea. Linguistic Typology 1(3): 347-386; Donohue, Mark. 2005. Tone and the Trans New Guinea languages (Kaji ed., ILCAA Tokyo); Donohue, Mark. 2012. The shape and spread of tone (Lincom).
sources.note: No mention of Burmeso/Taurap/Mamberamo in any of the three prosody surveys by the language's describer.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975a. Languages of Irian Jaya: checklist, preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics B-31 (Taurap = no. 151, Bromley wordlist).

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975b. Isolates: Irian Jaya [2.15.2.3 Taurap (or Borumeso)]. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1, 887-889. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.note: Nothing; p. 889: 'Nothing is known of the grammatical structure of Taurap.' Only lexical comparisons and four pronouns.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of Northwest New Guinea. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The languages and linguistics of the New Guinea area: a comprehensive guide (World of Linguistics 4), 433-568. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
